equation (0.1) describes the surface (averaged along the thickness δ(x)) magnetization induced
in a thin plate of width L of a ferromagnetic material with susceptibility κ by a transverse
external magnetic ﬁeld with a tangential component f(x). In this case, p(x) = κδ(x)/L. In
two-dimensional mechanics [K] equation (0.1) is the main tool in the study of contact problems
and calculations of stiﬀeners. Equation (0.1) can be considered as the potential theory equation
for the following boundary value problem

Boundary value problems of the type (0.2), (0.3) arise from general three-dimensional problems,
when one of the parameters of the domain (or of the surface) becomes “thin”.
As a rule, p(x) ⩾0, this function can vanish only at the ends of the interval. In general,
the potential theory equations for boundary value problems (0.2), (0.3) contain hypersingular
operators. In problem (0.2) this is the normal derivative of the double layer potential, and in
problem (0.3) this is the second tangential derivative of the single layer potential. However, the
degeneracy at the ends of the coeﬃcient p(x) facing the integral operator smooths out such a
singularity. In particular, if p(x) = (1 −x2)p0(x) and p0(±1) ̸= 0, ∞, then the operator that
corresponds to the second term in (0.1) is simply singular.
Usually it is not possible to solve the Prandtl equation exactly1. Therefore, the main literature
concerning applications is devoted to the search for convenient numerical schemes. One of the
most popular schemes is the Multopp method. A signiﬁcant part of the monograph [K] is devoted
to the justiﬁcation of this method. However, the conditions under which the Multopp method
is justiﬁed are too restrictive (for example, the function

Thus, a rigorous functional study of the Prandtl equation under natural (from the point of
view of physical applications) conditions on the coeﬃcient p(x) is very relevant.

0.3. Main results. We study problem (0.1) assuming that the coeﬃcient p(x) is a positive
function on (−1, 1), it may vanish for x = ±1, but the order of zeros is not higher than the ﬁrst
degree (see condition (1.2) on V (x) = p(x)−1 below). This case includes interesting from the
practical point of view examples of triangular wing of an airplane and a composite wing with a
chord break of ﬁrst kind.

for studying the problem on a ﬁnite interval. Therefore, investigating regularity of the solution,
we use a special integral transformation P on the interval, which was introduced and studied in

open [AP, P3]. The deﬁnition and the main properties of P are described in Section 2. We
introduce the interpolational scale of spaces eHs(−1, 1), s ⩾0, in terms of the transform P.

Abstract: Solvability and regularity of the solution of the Dirichlet problem for the Prandtl equation u(x) p(x) −1 2π Z 1 −1 u′(t) t −x dt = f(x) is studied. It is assumed that p(x) is a positive function on (−1, 1) such that sup (1−x2) p(x) < ∞. We introduce the scale of spaces e Hs(−1, 1) in terms of the special integral transformation on the interval (−1, 1). We obtain theorem about existence and uniqueness of the solution in the classes e Hs(−1, 1) with 0 ⩽s ⩽1. In particular, for s = 1 the result is as follows: if r1/2f ∈L2, then r−1/2u, r1/2u′ ∈L2, where r(x) = 1 −x2.
